title: Writing to Roosevelt and becoming a WPA conductor
summary: Randolph wrote to the President, got an answer from Steve Early, and was assigned an A-1 conductor on the WPA music project.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Well, I came back and I -- let's see, now, oh, yes, right. Franklin Delano was President, wasn't he?

Yes. That was during the WPA. And I got in the wind of this WPA and this big mammoth program was coming off. So I wrote to the President for the qualifications that I had and so on. I got a chance to be the supervisor of a union.
Excuse me just a minute. Supervisor of a union band?
That was better known by the Works Progress Administration, because they had the letters WPA.
A lot of people didn't like to hear that WPA. They didn't like that. They would rather people for you to say Work Progress Administration, 24 sound big.
But when you say WPA, that's kind of cheapened cheating them, like, you know.
Yeah, it had a bad reputation.

Yeah. So -- and a lot of times, for me to get back at the boys, when I would say, ladies and gentlemen, I says, this orchestra that you're about to hear, they're sponsored by the WPA, and the boys would get mad, you know.
